messages:
Sasha: @channel heads-up — ACME reporting a burst of 5xx/504s against hosted inference beginning ~15:14 UTC. They say a marketing campaign triggered a spike and now user flows are failing.

Jordan: saw alerts. request rate jumped ~18x for ~2 minutes. Gateway 504s line up with a gap where no upstream pod was Ready.

Priya: customer note: "we started seeing 20-40% 5xx in the 15:14-15:20 window, retries caused session issues" — they want a root cause and immediate mitigation.

Ethan: pulled gateway + runtime logs, snippets below: 
```
2026-03-14T15:14:22Z [gateway] upstream request timed out after 30s -> 504
2026-03-14T15:14:23Z [runtime] kv-cache allocate failed: no ready replica
```
Looks like the gateway waited then gave up while runtime had no Ready replicas.

Sasha: k8s metrics show backlog in queue. HPA CPU target fired but new pods weren't Ready fast enough. Could be node coldstart + model warmup.

Jordan: can someone check KEDA ScaledObject and scaler polling? We rely on KEDA for bursty tenants.

Ethan: grabbing the ScaledObject — it's using prometheus trigger with pollInterval: 30s and cooldown: 300s. For short, high-intensity bursts that's slow. Also HPA has stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300.

Priya: ACME confirms they sent a short blast of concurrent chat completions. No auth failures or billing errors reported.

Liz: CS needs wording for customer: what mitigation did we apply and what's next?

Ethan: immediate mitigation options I recommend (and what we applied):
- set minReplicas for ACME's tenant pool from 0 -> 2 to avoid all-cold starts
- deploy a canary ScaledObject with pollInterval=5s and cooldown=60s for this pool to speed scaler reaction (tradeoff: more control-plane ops)
- apply temporary per-tenant throttling/rate-limit to smooth incoming burst

Jordan: applied with Ethan: patched deployment to minReplicas=2 and applied a canary ScaledObject. Also added a short-term tenant rate-limit.

Sasha: please paste the kubectl commands used for audit.

Ethan: commands used: 
```
kubectl patch deployment inference-pool-acme -p '{"spec":{"replicas":2}}'
kubectl apply -f scaledobject-acme-canary.yaml  # pollInterval:5s cooldown:60s
kubectl annotate deployment inference-pool-acme redwood.com/temporary-throttle=true
```

Jordan: after new pods became Ready the 504s fell back to baseline within ~2 minutes. ACME confirms errors stopped.

Sasha: good catch. Root contributors seem to be: node provisioning delay (~40-60s), model warmup (init steps ~10-15s), and conservative scaler poll/stabilization settings.

Ethan: I reproduced in staging:
1) bombard /v1/chat/complete with 200 concurrent requests
2) observe KEDA poll -> scaler create -> new pods schedule
3) new pods spend ~12s in init pulling model, then become Ready ~30-50s after scale request; gateway times out earlier

Captured staging timing: 
```
[15:14:20] 200 concurrent connections start
[15:14:22] KEDA polls and requests scale: replicas 0->8
[15:14:26] cloud-provisioner: launching node
[15:14:34] pod init: model pull/warmup ~12s
[15:14:46] pod Ready
[15:14:48] downstream traffic success
```

Priya: so cold nodes + warmup window + slow scaler reaction = queued requests hitting gateway timeout. Nothing in billing/auth looked wrong.

Liz: CS message to ACME: "We've applied temporary mitigations (min replicas + throttling) and are doing a deeper fix. We'll update by EOD." They asked for ETA on a permanent solution.

Jordan: proposed remediation roadmap:
- short term (hrs): default safer ScaledObject template for tenant pools (pollInterval=10s, cooldown=90s), require nonzero minReplicas for customers with burst profiles
- medium (days): HPA patch to include external queue-length metric so CPU-only HPA doesn't miss request spikes
- longer (2-3 weeks): runtime warmup improvements — pre-warmed KV snapshots, faster model load, or an early-readiness signal with internal warmup queueing

Ethan: other notes: add an alert when "scale_request_pending > 45s" (scaler requested X replicas but no new Ready pods within window) to page oncall. Also tag gateway 504s with scaling_event_id for faster triage.

Jordan: opened PR for ScaledObject templates and defaults: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/4123 (draft) — sets pollInterval 10s for burst pools and recommends cooldown 90s.

Sasha: created incident ticket (P2) and assigned follow-ups: eng-runtime (warmup optimizations), eng-sre (KEDA/HPA defaults + alert), product (tenant burst SLAs/minReplica guidance), devex (docs).

Ethan: technical suggestion — snapshot KV-cache and mount during pod start to cut warmup from ~12s to <3s. Also consider prefetching model shards when node provisioning starts.

Priya: ACME: "Thanks, errors are gone for now. Please keep us posted." :thumbsup:

Sasha: closing this slack escalation thread. We'll follow up in the incident doc with timelines, root cause, mitigations and PR links.

Deploy Bot: deployment inference-pool-acme patched by Jordan at 15:24 UTC.

Jordan: follow-up: I'll prepare an HPA + external metric proposal and add the queue-length metric exporter instrumentation to the ingress.

Sasha: good. Keep updates here and paste the incident doc link when ready.
